definition_zh: 网站；网页集合；（一个域下的）站点
definition_en: a set of connected pages on the internet, usually belonging to one person or organisation
core_image: 一张网把许多房间连起来，每个房间门口挂着一块招牌
scene: 小书店的柜台旁贴着二维码，顾客扫开就能看到全部书目。The bookshop's website lists every title it has in stock.
sceneCN: 这里 website 是「网站」（第 1 个义项：互联网上相互连接的一系列页面）；句意为这家书店的网站列出了所有库存书目。门上挂招牌的连片房间，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 截短形式，义为「站点；场地」
复合词，义为「网站管理员」
本词的第一部分，义为「网；万维网」

senses.title: A set of connected pages
senses.titleCN: 网站：互相链接的一组页面
senses.definition: a group of connected pages on the internet that share one address
senses.definitionCN: 互联网上共用同一地址、彼此相连的一组页面
senses.example: The museum's website has a virtual tour of every hall.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的网站上有每个展厅的虚拟导览。
senses.why: web names the linking and site names the place; a website is a place built out of links.
senses.whyCN: web 指相互连接，site 指地点；website 就是由链接搭成的一个地方。

senses.title: An organisation's online home
senses.titleCN: 机构网站：组织在网络上的门面
senses.definition: the online presence of a company, school or public body, where information is published
senses.definitionCN: 公司、学校或公共机构在网络上发布信息的所在
senses.example: Apply through the university website before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 请在截止日期之前通过大学网站申请。
senses.why: A site is a plot of ground; the digital plot is where an organisation keeps its public face.
senses.whyCN: site 本是一块地；数字的「地」就是机构摆放门面的地方。

senses.title: A commercial shop online
senses.titleCN: 网上店铺：可下单选购的站点
senses.definition: a website used for selling goods or services, with pages for browsing and buying
senses.definitionCN: 用于出售商品或服务、可浏览下单的网站
senses.example: Their website takes orders until midnight and ships the next day.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的网站接单到午夜，第二天发货。
senses.why: The site turns into a counter: browsing pages leads to a basket and a payment, and the ground becomes a shop floor.
senses.whyCN: 站点变成了柜台：浏览页面通向购物篮与付款，那块「地」也就成了店面。

senses.title: One address, many pages
senses.titleCN: 一个地址下的整个站点
senses.definition: used of the whole collection of pages under a single domain name
senses.definitionCN: 指单一域名下的全部页面集合
senses.example: The old website is still online, though no one updates it.
senses.exampleCN: 旧网站仍然在线，尽管已经没人更新了。
senses.why: The plural pages are gathered under one name, and that name is the website as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 众多页面被收在一个名字之下，那个名字就是作为整体的网站。

senses.title: As a shortened form
senses.definition: in everyday speech often shortened to site, especially with a modifier
senses.definitionCN: 口语中常简写为 site，尤与修饰语连用
senses.example: Check the site for the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 去网站上看新的时间表。
senses.why: Speech shortens what print once spelled in two words, and site alone carries the whole meaning in context.
senses.whyCN: 口语把书面曾用两个词写的东西缩短，而 site 单用在语境中已含全部意思。

intro.en: Website is a late twentieth-century compound of web, from Old English, and site, from Latin.
intro.cn: website 是二十世纪后期的复合词，由古英语的 web 与拉丁语的 site 合成。

items.en: Web meant a woven cloth, and later the net of a spider; the sense of connected links came naturally.
items.cn: web 原指织成的布，后指蛛网；由此自然生出「相互链接」之义。

items.en: Situs meant 'a position, a site', from sinere 'to let, to place'; English site came through French.
items.cn: situs 意为「位置、地点」，出自 sinere「放置」；英语 site 经法语而来。

items.en: The World Wide Web was named at CERN around 1989, and web was quickly applied to the linked documents.
items.cn: 万维网约在 1989 年于欧洲核子研究中心命名，web 很快被用在这些相互链接的文档上。

items.en: Website was formed by joining web and site; the exact first printed use is uncertain.
items.cn: website 由 web 与 site 拼接而成，确切首次印行年代不确定。

items.en: The word replaced older phrases such as web site, and site alone now usually means the same thing.
items.cn: 这个词取代了 web site 等较早写法，如今单说 site 通常也指同一事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers web words that are easily confused with it; the near-meaning group gathers online places and their parts.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与之混淆的 web 类词；近义组收网络场所及其组成部分。

entries.definition: One single page inside a website.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网页」，是网站中的单独一页。

entries.definition: The network of linked documents, or a spider's net.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「万维网、网」，即互链文档构成的网络或蛛网。

entries.definition: The person who runs and updates a site.
The ability to see, or something seen; not related.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视力、景象」，与 site 同音但无关。

entries.definition: The short form of website; also any piece of ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网站」（website 的简写），也指任何一块地。

entries.definition: One screen of content within a site.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「页面」，是站点内的一屏内容。

entries.definition: A program on a device, which may replace a website.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「应用」，其功能可以替代网站。

entries.definition: A large site that gathers links and services for users.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门户网站」，集中提供链接与服务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English web and Latin situs, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 web 与拉丁语 situs，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: web is the linking, site is the place: a website is a place made of links.
normal.cn: web 是连接，site 是地点：website 就是用链接搭起的地方。

normal.en: A webpage is one page; a website is all the pages at once.
normal.cn: webpage 是一页，website 是全部页面加在一起。

normal.en: Every website has an address, just as a site has a location.
normal.cn: 每个网站都有地址，正如一块地有位置。

normal.en: Visit a website is the usual verb; you do not 'look' a website.
normal.cn: 常用动词是 visit；不能说 look a website。

normal.en: The short form site is used freely in speech.
normal.cn: 口语中常直接用简写 site。

abstract.en: Picture many rooms joined by corridors with a sign on every door: the corridors are the web, the rooms are the site.
abstract.cn: 想象许多房间由走廊相连，每扇门上挂着招牌：走廊是 web，房间群是 site。

abstract.en: The word joins an old cloth image to a very old idea of a place, and the result is a place without ground.
abstract.cn: 这个词把古老的布料意象接到同样古老的「地点」观念上，结果是一个没有土地的地点。

abstract.en: One address, many pages: the word is singular because the whole is one place.
abstract.cn: 一个地址，许多页面：这个词用单数，因为整体是一处地方。

examples.en: The school website posts the exam timetable every term.
examples.cn: 学校网站每学期都会发布考试时间表。

examples.en: She built her own website to sell the cloth she weaves.
examples.cn: 她自建网站出售自己织的布。

examples.en: Please check the website for the opening hours.
examples.cn: 开放时间请查看网站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网（web）下的赛特（site）」——网上搭起的一座赛特城：网站

root: 由现代英语 web（古英语「织网」，万维网）与 site（拉丁语 situs「位置」，经法语）在二十世纪九十年代拼合而成；相关词有 webpage、webmaster。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of website move from a set of linked pages, to an organisation's online home, to a shop, to one whole domain, and finally to the short spoken form.
sensesIntro.cn: website 的五个义项从相互链接的页面，到机构的网络门面，到网店，到整个域名下的站点，最后是口语简写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rooms joined by corridors, a sign on every door.
core.cn: 核心意象：由走廊相连的房间，每扇门上挂着招牌。

branches.en: LINK LINE: pages joined together under one address.
branches.cn: 链接线：同一地址下彼此的页面相连。

branches.en: HOME LINE: an organisation's public face online.
branches.cn: 门面线：机构在网络上的公开门面。

branches.en: SHOP LINE: a site you can buy from.
branches.cn: 店铺线：可以下单购买的站点。

branches.en: SHORT LINE: speech cuts it to site.
branches.cn: 简写线：口语中缩为 site。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a webpage is one room, a website is the building.
branches.cn: 对照线：webpage 是一个房间，website 是整栋楼。

intro.en: Website is a modern compound whose two halves come from very different places.
intro.cn: website 是现代复合词，其两半来自很不一样的地方。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half has a verifiable Latin origin: situs.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半有可查的拉丁语来源：situs。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 webpage 与 webmaster。

items.example: It forms web-based in related use.

definition_zh: 杂草；野草；菸草（口语）；除草
definition_en: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted, and also to remove such plants
core_image: 菜畦里一丛比菜苗还壮的野草，被人一把连根拔起
scene: 雨后的菜畦里，野草长得比菜苗还高，母亲蹲下把它们一株株拔起来。After the rain the weeds stood taller than the young vegetables, so we pulled them out.
sceneCN: 这里 weed 是「杂草」（第 1 个义项：长在不该长地方的野生植物）；句意为雨后野草比菜苗还高，我们把它拔掉。比菜苗还壮、被连根拔起的那丛草就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A plant in the wrong place
senses.definition: a wild plant growing where people do not want it
senses.definitionCN: 长在人们不需要的地方的野生植物
senses.example: Dandelions are a weed in a lawn and a flower in a meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 蒲公英在草坪上是杂草，在草甸上是花。
senses.why: This is the core sense, and it depends on place rather than species.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，取决于位置而非种类。

senses.title: To remove such plants
senses.definition: to pull out or cut unwanted plants from a garden or field
senses.definitionCN: 从园圃或田地里拔掉或割掉不受欢迎的植物
senses.example: They weeded the beds before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们到来之前，他们把花坛的草清干净了。
senses.why: Once the noun named the plant, the verb named the work.
senses.whyCN: 名词指草之后，动词就指拔草这件事。

senses.title: To remove unwanted things or people
senses.definition: to get rid of weak or unwanted members from a group
senses.definitionCN: 从群体中清掉弱的或不需要的成员
senses.example: The first round weeds out the weakest entries.
senses.exampleCN: 第一轮会淘汰最弱的参赛作品。
senses.why: Pulling weak plants out of a bed gives the image for clearing a list.
senses.whyCN: 把弱苗从苗床里拔掉，为清理名单提供了意象。

senses.title: Tobacco, in informal use
senses.definition: an old slang word for tobacco or a cigarette
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中指菸草或香烟
senses.example: He stepped outside for a weed.
senses.exampleCN: 他走到外面抽支烟。
senses.why: This slang sense is old and has almost disappeared from polite speech.
senses.whyCN: 这一俚语义已陈旧，在正式场合几乎绝迹。

senses.title: A troublesome person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing seen as a nuisance, in slang
senses.definitionCN: 口语中令人讨厌的人或事
senses.example: That old car is a weed of a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车真是台麻烦机器。
senses.why: Something that grows where it is not wanted and will not go away suits both plants and pests.
senses.whyCN: 在不该生长的地方长起来又除不掉的东西，既像草也像麻烦。

intro.en: Weed is an Old English word for a harmful herb, and it once carried the sense of something poisonous or worthless.
intro.cn: weed 是古英语中表示有害草木的词，曾带有「有毒、无用」的意味。

items.en: Wēod meant a herb, especially a harmful one growing among crops.
items.cn: wēod 意为草木，尤指长在作物间的有害草木。

items.en: Related forms in Dutch and German also mean weed, so the sense is very old.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语中的相关形式也表示杂草，可见这个意义很古老。

items.en: Spelling settled as weed and the garden sense became fixed.
items.cn: 拼写定为 weed，园艺义随之固定。

items.en: Weed out grew from garden work into any clearing of a group.
items.cn: weed out 从园艺劳动扩展到对任何群体的清理。

items.en: Slang uses for tobacco and for a tiresome person came and mostly went.
items.cn: 指菸草与讨厌之人的俚语用法出现过，又多半消散。

note.en: The first group shares the weed word, the second names plants and clearing work.
note.cn: 第一组与 weed 同词同源，第二组指植物与清理工作。

entries.definition: Full of weeds, or thin and weak.
Plant-like growth in the sea.
A substance that kills weeds.
The work of removing weeds.
The common green ground plant, wanted on lawns.
Any living green thing that grows in soil.
A plant used for food or medicine.
Loosening soil and cutting weeds with a hoe.

normalIntro.en: A weed is not a kind of plant but a plant in the wrong place, which is why the verb can also mean to clear a list.
normalIntro.cn: 杂草不是某个种类，而是长错地方的植物，所以动词也能表示清理名单。

normal.en: Weed is both the plant and the pulling of it.
normal.cn: weed 既是草，也是拔草。

normal.en: Weed out means remove the weak ones.
normal.cn: weed out 意为剔除弱者。

normal.en: Weedy grounds are full of weeds; a weedy person is thin.
normal.cn: weedy 地面满是草，weedy 的人很瘦。

normal.en: Seaweed is not a garden pest at all.
normal.cn: seaweed 根本不是园中害虫。

normal.en: Weedkiller is what stops you weeding by hand.
normal.cn: weedkiller 让你不必动手拔草。

abstract.en: Picture a thistle standing higher than lettuce.
abstract.cn: 想一株飞蓟比生菜还高。

abstract.en: Feel the root come free with a quick tug.
abstract.cn: 感受一拽根部就松脱。

abstract.en: Smell the crushed green on your hands.
abstract.cn: 闻手上碾碎的青草味。

examples.en: The path is overgrown with weeds.
examples.cn: 这条小路上长满杂草。

examples.en: He spent the morning weeding the vegetable beds.
examples.cn: 他花了一上午给菜畦除草。

examples.en: The test is meant to weed out careless applicants.
examples.cn: 这项测试意在淘汰粗心的申请者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威得」——威得大叔蹲在菜地，一根根拔得干净，说这些都是抢营养的杂草。

root: 古英语 wēod（草本，尤指有害草木）→ 中古英语 weed；同源词有 weedy、seaweed。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a plant out of place, becomes the work of removing it, then any clearing of unwanted members.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从长错地方的植物出发，成为清除它的劳动，再指任何对多余成员的清理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weed pulled up by the root.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株被连根拔起的草。

branches.en: The plant branch: dandelions in a lawn.
branches.cn: 植物分支：草坪上的蒲公英。

branches.en: The work branch: beds weeded before guests came.
branches.cn: 劳动分支：客人来前清好的花坛。

branches.en: The bed branch: beds weeded before guests came.
branches.cn: 苗床分支：客人来前清好的花坛。

branches.en: The clearing branch: a test that weeds out the careless.
branches.cn: 清理分支：淘汰粗心者的测试。

branches.en: The slang branch: an old word for a cigarette or a nuisance.
branches.cn: 俚语分支：旧时指香烟或讨厌之物。

intro.en: Weed takes the ordinary English endings for its plural and its verb forms.
intro.cn: weed 的复数与动词形式采用普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

items.meaning: more than one, or he weeds

definition_zh: 每周的；一周一次的；名词：周刊；副词：每周一次
definition_en: happening or produced once every week, or a magazine that appears once a week
core_image: 日历上每一排的开头都夹着同一张便签，被反复圈了四圈
scene: 镇上的面包店门口贴着手写告示，每逢周六早上折扣。The shop holds a weekly market on Saturday mornings.
sceneCN: 这里 weekly 是「每周的」（第 1 个义项：每七天发生一次）；句意为这家店每周六早上办集市。日历上七天被圈成一轮，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：每周的；一周一次的

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根名词，义为「星期；一周」
加前缀 bi- 构成，义为「两周一次的」或「每周两次的」，常需说明

senses.title: Happening every week
senses.titleCN: 每周的：每七天发生一次
senses.definition: happening or done once every week
senses.definitionCN: 每七天发生或做一次
senses.example: The team has a weekly meeting on Monday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每周一下午开周会。
senses.why: The suffix -ly here turns the period into a frequency: week plus -ly means once per week.
senses.whyCN: 此处的后缀 -ly 把时间段变成频率：week 加 -ly 即「每周一次」。

senses.title: Of a weekly amount
senses.titleCN: 按周的：以一周为单位的数量
senses.definition: calculated or paid by the week rather than by the month
senses.definitionCN: 按周而非按月计算的数目
senses.example: Her weekly income barely covers the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周的收入勉强够付房租。
senses.why: The period works as a unit here: the pay packet arrives every seventh day.
senses.whyCN: 这里把周期当单位：薪金每隔七天到手一次。

senses.title: A magazine or paper
senses.titleCN: 周刊：每周出一期的刊物
senses.definition: a newspaper or magazine published once a week
senses.definitionCN: 每周出版一期的报纸或杂志
senses.example: The village weekly prints little more than notices and recipes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份乡村周刊几乎只登通告和菜谱。
senses.why: A publication takes its name from its rhythm, so the adjective becomes a noun.
senses.whyCN: 出版物以其节律为名，于是形容词转成了名词。

senses.title: As an adverb
senses.definition: used as an adverb meaning once a week
senses.definitionCN: 作副词使用，意为「每周一次地」
senses.example: The bins are collected weekly in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天垃圾每周收一次。
senses.why: The same word can answer the question how often without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词形式不变，就能回答「多久一次」的问题。

senses.title: In fixed phrases
senses.titleCN: 固定说法：如 on a weekly basis
senses.definition: in phrases such as on a weekly basis, meaning with a weekly rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on a weekly basis 等短语，表示按周进行的节律
senses.example: The results are reviewed on a weekly basis, not daily.
senses.exampleCN: 这些结果按周复查，而不是按天。
senses.why: Formal writing dresses the same rhythm in a prepositional phrase.
senses.whyCN: 正式写作把同一种节律装进一个介词短语里。

intro.en: Weekly is a native English formation: the Germanic noun week plus the very common -ly ending.
intro.cn: weekly 是本族英语构词：日耳曼语名词 week 加上极为常见的 -ly 词尾。

items.en: Wicu meant 'a week', with the sense of a turn or a succession of days.
items.cn: wicu 意为「一周」，带有「一轮、一连串日子」的意思。

items.en: German Woche and Dutch week are cognates, and the root may have meant a turn or a change.
items.cn: 德语 Woche 与荷兰语 week 同源，词根原义可能与「轮换、变动」有关。

items.en: The suffix -lic meant 'having the body or form of', and became modern -ly.
items.cn: -lic 后缀意为「具有……的形态」，后来变成现代的 -ly。

items.en: Wekely was used both for 'once a week' and for 'lasting a week'.
items.cn: 中古英语 wekely 既表示「每周一次」，也表示「持续一周」。

items.en: The noun use for a weekly paper or magazine dates from the eighteenth century; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 指周报、周刊的名词用法始于十八世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other frequency words in -ly; the near-meaning group gathers periods and publications.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 -ly 表频率的词；近义组收周期与刊物类词。

entries.definition: Happening every day; also a daily paper.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每日的」，也指日报。

entries.definition: Happening once a month; also a monthly magazine.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每月的」，也指月刊。

entries.definition: Happening once a year; the same -ly frequency ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每年的」，用同样表频率的 -ly。

entries.definition: In a weak way; a near homophone of weekly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「虚弱地」，与 weekly 读音极近。

entries.definition: The period of seven days behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星期」，是形容词背后的时间段。

entries.definition: A magazine published at regular intervals of any length.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「期刊」，出版间隔可长可短。

entries.definition: Happening every two weeks; the British partner of weekly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每两周的」，是英式说法中 weekly 的伙伴。

entries.definition: A regular way of doing things, without fixing the period.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「常规」，不固定周期长度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wicu and -lic, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wicu 与 -lic，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: week plus -ly: the period becomes the frequency.
normal.cn: week 加 -ly：时间段变成了频率。

normal.en: Daily, weekly, monthly, yearly line up in the same family.
normal.cn: daily、weekly、monthly、yearly 排在同一家族里。

normal.en: A weekly is a paper; a daily is a paper too, so the noun works the same way.
normal.cn: weekly 是周刊，daily 是日报，名词化的方式相同。

normal.en: Twice weekly means two times in one week, not two weeks.
normal.cn: twice weekly 指一周两次，不是两周一次。

normal.en: Weakly differs by one letter and means without strength.
normal.cn: weakly 只差一个字母，意为无力地。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with every seventh square circled in the same colour: that repeated circle is weekly.
abstract.cn: 想象一张日历，每隔七格就用同一种颜色圈一次：那一再重画的圈就是 weekly。

abstract.en: The word measures rhythm, not length of time, which is why it works as adjective, noun and adverb.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量的是节律而不是时长，所以能作形容词、名词和副词。

abstract.en: A weekly habit is small but relentless: seven days always come back.
abstract.cn: 每周一次的习惯看似不大却不停歇：七天总会再来。

examples.en: The lab publishes a weekly report on air quality.
examples.cn: 实验室每周发布空气质量报告。

examples.en: He buys a weekly on Fridays and reads it over the weekend.
examples.cn: 他每周五买一份周刊，周末读完。

examples.en: The garden is watered weekly in dry weather.
examples.cn: 干旱时花园每周浇一次水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围（wee）克（k）里（ly）」——每七天围成一圈，一周一轮：每周的

root: 由古英语 wicu「一周」加后缀 -lic（现代 -ly）构成；同源频率词有 daily、monthly、yearly。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weekly take one period of seven days and use it as a rhythm, an amount, a publication, an adverb, and a fixed phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: weekly 的五个义项把七天这一段当作节律、数额、刊物、副词用法，以及一个固定短语来使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar with every seventh square circled in the same colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上每隔七格被同色圈起的一格。

branches.en: RHYTHM LINE: the same event returns every seventh day.
branches.cn: 节律线：同一件事每七天回来一次。

branches.en: AMOUNT LINE: money counted by the week.
branches.cn: 数额线：以周为单位计算的金额。

branches.en: PAPER LINE: a publication keeps the weekly beat.
branches.cn: 刊物线：一份出版物守着每周的节拍。

branches.en: ADVERB LINE: no preposition needed, the word says how often.
branches.cn: 副词线：无需介词，这个词直接说明频率。

branches.en: PHRASE LINE: on a weekly basis formalises the same rhythm.
branches.cn: 短语线：on a weekly basis 把同一节律说得更正式。

intro.en: Weekly is a Germanic noun plus a Germanic suffix, with no Latin ingredient.
intro.cn: weekly 是日耳曼语名词加日耳曼语后缀，不含拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.meaning: of a kind; in that manner

definition_zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使烦恼
definition_en: to measure how heavy something is, to have a stated weight, and to think carefully about choices
core_image: 老式天平两端各放一只盘，指针在刻度间来回摆动最后停住
scene: 集市上卖水果的老板把袋子放上秤盘，指针一晃，最后停在一个数上，他报出价来。The seller put the bag on the scale to weigh it and waited for the needle to settle.
sceneCN: 这里 weigh 是「称重」（第 1 个义项：测量某物有多重）；句意为摊主把袋子放上秤，等指针停稳。两端摆动的天平与指针就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 称…的重量；重达；权衡；使忧心

senses.title: To measure weight
senses.definition: to find out how heavy something is, using a scale
senses.definitionCN: 用秤查明某物有多重
senses.example: The nurse weighed the baby at every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每次来访都给婴儿称重。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the balance answers a question of heaviness.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：天平回答「有多重」的问题。

senses.title: To have a stated weight
senses.definition: to be of a particular heaviness
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个特定的重量
senses.example: This parcel weighs almost two kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包裹重近两公斤。
senses.why: The verb takes the weight as its own measure, so no object is needed.
senses.whyCN: 动词自身带上重量，因此不需要宾语。

senses.title: To think about choices
senses.definition: to compare facts or options carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定前仔细比较事实或选项
senses.example: The committee weighed the risks before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在投票前权衡了风险。
senses.why: A balance holds two pans, and a mind holds two options the same way.
senses.whyCN: 天平托着两只盘，头脑也同样托着两个选择。

senses.title: To be a burden on someone
senses.definition: to trouble or oppress a person’s mind
senses.definitionCN: 使某人心里烦恼、沉重
senses.example: The decision weighed on her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定压在她心上好几周。
senses.why: Something heavy presses down, so worry is said to weigh on a mind.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的东西会向下压，于是忧虑被说成压在心头。

senses.title: To raise a ship’s anchor
senses.definition: of a ship, to lift the anchor before sailing
senses.definitionCN: 指船在启航前把锚拉起
senses.example: The fleet weighed anchor at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船队在黎明起锚。
senses.why: A phrase from sailing, kept because anchor and balance share the idea of lifting.
senses.whyCN: 这是航海用语，因为起锚与天平共通「抬起」的意象而保留。

intro.en: Weigh comes from Old English wegan, to carry or to lift, the same root that gives wagon and the Latin vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: weigh 来自古英语 wegan（搬运、抬起），与 wagon 及拉丁语 vehere（运载）同根。

items.en: The root meant to move or carry a load, and weighing was done by lifting and comparing.
items.cn: 这一词根意为移动或承载，古时称量靠抬起并比较。

items.en: Wegan meant to carry, to lift and to weigh, all in one verb.
items.cn: wegan 一名兼指搬运、抬起与称量。

items.en: The spelling weigh appeared, and the past form became weighed under French-influenced habits.
items.cn: 拼写 weigh 出现，过去式在法语影响下成为 weighed。

items.en: The weighing of evidence extended the word to judgement and decision.
items.cn: 权衡证据把词义扩展到判断与决断。

items.en: Weight, the noun, came from the same root and now names the thing measured.
items.cn: 名词 weight 出自同根，如今指被测量的那份东西。

note.en: The first group shares the weigh root and shape, the second the words used in measuring and deciding.
note.cn: 第一组与 weigh 同根形近，第二组是测量与决断中的近义词。

entries.definition: How heavy a thing is, or a piece of metal used to weigh.
Heavy, or serious and important.
The act of measuring or judging.
A road or method, the same sound.
To find the size or amount of something.
To think about something before deciding.
To judge the value or quality of something.
To load someone with a heavy duty or worry.

normalIntro.en: Start with the balance, then let it tilt into decisions and into worry.
normalIntro.cn: 先看天平，再让它倾斜出去，成为决断与忧虑。

normal.en: Weigh is the verb; weight is the noun.
normal.cn: weigh 是动词，weight 是名词。

normal.en: Weigh about ten kilos needs no object.
normal.cn: weigh about ten kilos 不带宾语。

normal.en: Weigh the options means put each one on the balance.
normal.cn: weigh the options 就是把每个选择放上天平。

normal.en: Weigh on someone means press down on the mind.
normal.cn: weigh on someone 是压在某人心上。

normal.en: Weigh anchor is the opposite of drop anchor.
normal.cn: weigh anchor 与 drop anchor 相反。

abstract.en: Picture a needle swinging and dying away.
abstract.cn: 想指针摆动后慢慢停住。

abstract.en: Hear the small click of a brass weight set down.
abstract.cn: 听铜砝码落下时轻轻一响。

abstract.en: Feel one side sink and the other rise.
abstract.cn: 感受一头下沉、一头升起。

examples.en: Please weigh this parcel before you post it.
examples.cn: 寄之前请称一下这个包裹。

examples.en: She weighs less than she did last year.
examples.cn: 她比去年轻了些。

examples.en: You must weigh the cost against the benefit.
examples.cn: 你必须把成本与收益权衡一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂」——摊主喊一声「喂」，把袋子往秤上一放，看指针停在哪。

root: 日耳曼语词根（搬运、抬举）→ 古英语 wegan（搬、抬、称）→ weigh；同根词有 weight、wagon，拉丁语 vehere。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts at the balance, states a weight, then moves to weighing options, to weighing on a mind, and to lifting an anchor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从天平出发，报出重量，再转为权衡选择、压在心头，最后是起锚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale needle settling.
core.cn: 核心意象：停住的秤针。

branches.en: The measure branch: weighing a baby and weighing two kilos.
branches.cn: 测量分支：给婴儿称重与重两公斤。

branches.en: The judgement branch: comparing risks before a vote.
branches.cn: 判断分支：投票前比较风险。

branches.en: The burden branch: a decision that presses for weeks.
branches.cn: 负担分支：压了数周的决定。

branches.en: The sailing branch: anchor lifted at dawn.
branches.cn: 航海分支：黎明起锚。

branches.en: The scale and the mind share one image: two pans, then two choices.
branches.cn: 天平与头脑共用一个意象：两只盘，两个选择。

intro.en: Weigh takes regular endings and the noun weight from the same root.
intro.cn: weigh 用规则词尾，名词 weight 出自同一词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin vehere means to carry, and the table shows how the same image spread.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词 vehere 意为运载，拉丁表展示同一意象的扩散。

items.meaning: to carry, to lift, to weigh

definition_zh: 重量；体重；砝码；分量、重要性；负担
definition_en: how heavy something is, a heavy object used for weighing, or the importance and pressure that something carries
core_image: 秤盘往下一沉，指针稳稳停在一个刻度上
scene: 邮局柜台上的小秤被包裹压得沉下去，指针慢慢摆回中间。The parcel's weight pushed the scale well past one kilogram.
sceneCN: 这里 weight 是「重量」（第 1 个义项：物体有多重）；句意为包裹的重量让秤的读数远远超过一公斤。秤盘下沉、指针停稳，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：重量、体重；砝码；分量、重要性；负担
动词：加重于；使倾斜；权衡

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根动词，义为「称重；重达；权衡」
加后缀 -y 构成，义为「沉重的；重要的」
加后缀 -less 构成，义为「失重的；无重量的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「权重；加权」

senses.title: How heavy a thing is
senses.definition: the amount that something weighs, measured in kilograms or pounds
senses.definitionCN: 某物有多重，以公斤或磅计量
senses.example: The weight of the box made her put it down twice.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子太重，她不得不放下两次。
senses.why: The noun comes from the verb weigh, and both grow from a Germanic root for carrying.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自动词 weigh，两者都源自日耳曼语表示「承载」的词根。

senses.title: A piece of metal for weighing
senses.titleCN: 砝码：称量用的标准重物
senses.definition: a piece of metal of known mass, used with a balance or as a load in exercise
senses.definitionCN: 已知质量的金属块，用于天平称量或作为负重
senses.example: He added a small weight to the other pan.
senses.exampleCN: 他在另一边秤盘上加了一枚小砝码。
senses.why: A known amount of heaviness becomes a physical object you can pick up.
senses.whyCN: 已知的分量变成了可以拿在手里的实物。

senses.title: The body's weight
senses.definition: the heaviness of a person's body, often spoken of as rising or falling
senses.definitionCN: 人体有多重，常以增减来描述
senses.example: He lost weight during the long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的病中他瘦了不少。
senses.why: From the heaviness of any object the noun narrows to the body: body weight is simply how much you press on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 从任何物体的重，这个名词收窄到身体：体重就是你压在秤上的分量。

senses.title: Importance or influence
senses.definition: the importance, authority or influence that something carries
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所承载的重要性、权威或影响
senses.example: Her words carry weight in the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话在委员会里很有分量。
senses.why: The physical image is kept whole: important words are said to carry weight, as if they pressed down on the listener.
senses.whyCN: 物理意象被整体保留：有分量的言语被说成 carry weight，仿佛它们压在听者身上。

senses.title: A burden or pressure
senses.titleCN: 负担：压在身上的沉重感
senses.definition: a heavy load, physical or mental, that presses on someone
senses.definitionCN: 压在身上的沉重负担，可以是身体上的，也可以是心理上的
senses.example: The weight of the debt kept him awake.
senses.exampleCN: 债务的重压让他夜夜难眠。
senses.why: The same downward force becomes an image of worry: what presses on the mind is described as a weight.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向下之力成了忧虑的意象：压在心上的东西被说成 a weight。

intro.en: Weight is the noun of the verb weigh, and both go back to an Old English word for carrying.
intro.cn: weight 是动词 weigh 的名词形式，两者都可追溯到古英语表示「承载」的词。

items.en: Wegan meant 'to carry, to move, to weigh'; weighing was originally lifting a thing to feel it.
items.cn: wegan 意为「搬运、移动、称量」；最初的称重就是把东西提起来感受轻重。

items.en: German wiegen 'to weigh' and Dutch wegen are cognates of the same carrying root.
items.cn: 德语 wiegen 与荷兰语 wegen 是同一「承载」词根的同源词。

items.en: The noun gewiht meant 'weight', literally what has been lifted and measured.
items.cn: 名词 gewiht 意为「重量」，字面就是「被提起并称过的东西」。

items.en: The noun became weight, and the figurative sense of importance appeared early.
items.cn: 该名词演变为 weight，表示「重要性」的比喻义很早就出现了。

items.en: Medicine and sport fixed the body senses, while politics kept the sense of influence.
items.cn: 医学与运动固定了身体方面的用法，政治语境则保留了「影响力」义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the weigh family; the near-meaning group gathers heaviness, importance and burden words.
note.cn: 形近组收 weigh 一族词；近义组收重量、重要性与负担类词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to measure heaviness or think over a choice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「称重、权衡」，是本名词的词根。

entries.definition: Heavy, or serious and important.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「沉重的」，或「重大的」。

entries.definition: Having no apparent weight, as in orbit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失重的」，如轨道中的状态。

entries.definition: To stay until something happens; a homophone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「等待」，与 weight 同音。

entries.definition: The amount of matter in a body, fixed while weight can change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「质量」，指物质多少，而重量可变。

entries.definition: The quality of being heavy; plainer and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沉重」，更朴素也少技术味。

entries.definition: The state of mattering a lot; the plain word for the figurative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重要性」，是比喻义的平实说法。

entries.definition: A load carried, especially one that is hard to bear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「负担」，尤指难以承受的重负。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wegan and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wegan，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: weigh is the verb, weight is the noun: you weigh a parcel to find its weight.
normal.cn: weigh 是动词，weight 是名词：称包裹为了知道它的 weight。

normal.en: Lose weight and gain weight keep the body sense in motion.
normal.cn: lose weight 与 gain weight 让身体义保持动态。

normal.en: Carry weight means be listened to, as a heavy voice is hard to ignore.
normal.cn: carry weight 意为被人重视，因为沉重的声音难以忽略。

normal.en: A weight on a balance is a known heaviness you can hold.
normal.cn: 天平上的砝码就是一份可以拿在手里的已知重量。

normal.en: Wait is a homophone and means to stay; weight means heaviness.
normal.cn: wait 同音，意为停留；weight 意为沉重。

abstract.en: Picture one pan of a scale sinking: weight is whatever pulls the pan down.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一侧的秤盘下沉：重量就是把它往下拉的东西。

abstract.en: The same downward pull becomes influence in a meeting and pressure in a worried mind.
abstract.cn: 同一种下拉之力，在会议上成了影响力，在焦虑的心里成了压力。

abstract.en: Everything heavy can be measured, and everything important can be said to carry weight.
abstract.cn: 凡沉的东西都能测量，凡重要的事都能说「有分量」。

examples.en: The doctor recorded the baby's weight each month.
examples.cn: 医生每个月记录婴儿的体重。

examples.en: His opinion carries real weight with the board.
examples.cn: 他的意见在董事会里很有分量。

examples.en: She felt the weight of the decision for weeks.
examples.cn: 那个决定的重压让她好几周都难以轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wei）特（ght）」——喂饱了的秤盘特别沉：重量

root: 由古英语动词 wegan「搬、称」派生名词 gewiht「重量」，中古英语作 weight；同族词有 weigh、weighty、weightless。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weight run from the measured heaviness of a parcel, to a metal weight, to the body, to influence, and to the burden that presses on a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: weight 的五个义项从包裹被测出的重量，到金属砝码，到身体，到影响力，再到压在心里的重负。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pan of a scale sinking until the needle settles on a mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一侧下沉，直到指针停在某个刻度上。

branches.en: MEASURE LINE: parcels and bodies weighed on instruments.
branches.cn: 测量线：包裹与身体在器具上被称量。

branches.en: OBJECT LINE: a known heaviness becomes a metal block.
branches.cn: 实物线：已知的沉重变成一块金属。

branches.en: INFLUENCE LINE: a voice that is hard to ignore.
branches.cn: 影响线：难以忽略的声音。

branches.en: PRESSURE LINE: the same pull felt inside the mind.
branches.cn: 压力线：同一种下拉，在心里被感受到。

branches.en: CONTRAST: mass stays the same, weight can change with gravity.
branches.cn: 对照线：质量不变，重量会随重力改变。

intro.en: Weight is a native noun from the weighing verb, and its derivatives use ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: weight 是出自「称量」动词的本族名词，派生词用普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.

definition_zh: 奇怪的；怪异的；离奇的；（古）命运的
definition_en: very strange and hard to explain, often in a way that makes people uneasy
core_image: 街角的路灯忽明忽暗，路口站着一个人影，看不清脸
scene: 夜里回家时，楼道灯一间间亮起又灭掉，脚步声总在身后多一下，他回头看却没有人。That night the corridor felt weird; every light went out just behind him.
sceneCN: 这里 weird 是「奇怪的」（第 1 个义项：非常怪异、难以解释，且常令人不安）；句意为那晚走廊里感觉怪怪的，灯总在他身后熄灭。忽明忽暗的灯与看不清脸的人影就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Very strange and unsettling
senses.definition: unusual in a way that is hard to explain and slightly disturbing
senses.definitionCN: 异于寻常、难以解释且略带不安
senses.example: There was a weird smell in the empty flat.
senses.exampleCN: 空屋子里有一股怪味。
senses.why: This is the modern core: strange plus a slight shiver.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代核心义：奇怪外加一点发凉。

senses.title: Strange in an interesting way
senses.definition: strange in a way that is odd but engaging
senses.definitionCN: 怪得有趣、引人好奇
senses.example: The shop sells weird and wonderful lamps.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖各种离奇有趣的灯。
senses.why: The same strangeness can charm rather than chill, which gives the phrase weird and wonderful.
senses.whyCN: 同一种怪可以是迷人也可是骇人，于是有了 weird and wonderful。

senses.title: Behaving oddly
senses.definition: of a person, acting in an odd or puzzling way
senses.definitionCN: 指人行为反常、令人费解
senses.example: He has been weird all week, not answering messages.
senses.exampleCN: 他这一周都很古怪，消息也不回。
senses.why: The same strangeness turns outward, so odd behaviour carries the word of the uncanny.
senses.whyCN: 同一种怪转向人本身，于是古怪的行为也带上了这个诡异之词。

senses.title: Feeling unwell
senses.definition: in informal use, feeling faint or unwell
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指感到不适、发虚
senses.example: I felt weird after the second cup of coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 第二杯咖啡之后我觉得不太舒服。
senses.why: A body that feels strange is described with the word for anything strange.
senses.whyCN: 身体感觉不对劲，就用了形容任何怪异之物的词。

senses.title: Fateful, in older use
senses.definition: in old literature, having power over fate
senses.definitionCN: 古文学中指尖有掌控命运之力
senses.example: The weird sisters appear before the king.
senses.exampleCN: 命运三姐妹出现在国王面前。
senses.why: This is the original sense, from the noun weird meaning fate, later softened to fateful.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义，来自名词 weird（命运），后来淡化为「关乎命运的」。

intro.en: Weird first meant fate, from Old English wyrd, and the modern sense of strange grew out of the idea of a fateful, uncanny power.
intro.cn: weird 本义是「命运」，来自古英语 wyrd；现代的「奇怪」义由「带着命运感、超乎自然的力量」生长而来。

items.en: Wyrd meant fate or destiny, the power that decides what happens to a person.
items.cn: wyrd 意为命运，决定一个人遭遇何事的那个力量。

items.en: The root is the same as the verb become, so fate was the word for what turns out.
items.cn: 这一词根与动词 become 同源，命运便指最终成为的样子。

items.en: The weird sisters of fate were the three goddesses who spin a life’s thread.
items.cn: 中古英语中 the weird sisters 是纺出人生之线的三位女神。

items.en: In Macbeth the weird sisters are witches, and weird took on the sense of uncanny.
items.cn: 在《麦克白》里 the weird sisters 是女巫，weird 由此带上诡异之意。

items.en: The adjective weakened from uncanny to simply strange and odd.
items.cn: 这个形容词从诡异淡化为单纯的奇怪、古怪。

note.en: The first group is the weird family, the second the adjectives of strangeness.
note.cn: 第一组是 weird 词族，第二组是表示奇怪的形容词。

entries.definition: In a strange way.
The quality of being strange.
A person seen as strange.
Fate, the original sense.
The plain word for unfamiliar or odd.
Slightly unusual or peculiar.
Strange in a way that frightens.
Strange in a way that seems supernatural.

normalIntro.en: Remember the old sense first: weird was fate, and only later came to mean strange.
normalIntro.cn: 先记住旧义：weird 本来是命运，后来才变成「奇怪」。

normal.en: Weird is the adjective; weirdly and weirdness follow.
normal.cn: weird 是形容词，weirdly、weirdness 随之而来。

normal.en: A weirdo is a strange person, short and informal.
normal.cn: weirdo 是怪人，简短而口语。

normal.en: Weird and wonderful pairs oddness with charm.
normal.cn: weird and wonderful 把古怪与迷人配在一起。

normal.en: Feel weird means feel unwell, not see ghosts.
normal.cn: feel weird 是不舒服，不是见鬼。

normal.en: The weird sisters in Macbeth are the Three Witches.
normal.cn: 《麦克白》里的 weird sisters 就是三女巫。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp flickering above an empty corner.
abstract.cn: 想路灯在空街角上忽明忽暗。

abstract.en: Hear one extra footstep behind you.
abstract.cn: 听身后多出一步脚步。

abstract.en: Feel the small chill on the back of the neck.
abstract.cn: 感受后颈那一点涼。

examples.en: It is weird to see the square so empty.
examples.cn: 看到广场这么空，感觉很奇怪。

examples.en: She had a weird dream about a door in the sea.
examples.cn: 她做了一个怪梦，梦见海里有一扇门。

examples.en: The whole afternoon felt weird around him.
examples.cn: 他身边的整个下午都透着古怪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威德」——威德夜里回家，路灯一盏盏在身后灭掉，他说这真够怪的。

root: 古英语 wyrd（命运，同根于 become）→ 中古英语 weird sisters（命运三女神）→ 莎士比亚后转为「诡异」→ 现代「奇怪」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as fate, darkens into uncanny power, then lightens into ordinary strangeness.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从命运出发，变暗成诡异的力量，再变轻为平常的「奇怪」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp flickering over an empty corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：空街角上明灭的灯。

branches.en: The strange branch: a smell in an empty flat.
branches.cn: 怪异分支：空屋里的一股怪味。

branches.en: The charming branch: weird and wonderful lamps.
branches.cn: 迷人分支：离奇有趣的灯。

branches.en: The personal branch: queer behaviour and a body that feels odd.
branches.cn: 个人分支：古怪行为与不适的身体。

branches.en: The fate branch: the weird sisters of old literature.
branches.cn: 命运分支：旧文学里的命运姐妹。

branches.en: The charm and the fate branch: both keep the old shiver of the uncanny.
branches.cn: 迷人分支与命运分支：两者都留着那点古旧的诡异寒意。

intro.en: Weird is a bare adjective that takes the ordinary -ly, -ness and -o endings.
intro.cn: weird 是光杆形容词，采用普通的 -ly、-ness 与 -o 词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 焊接；熔接；使紧密结合；名词：焊接处
definition_en: to join pieces of metal by heating their edges until they melt together, or to unite things closely
core_image: 两块铁被高温烧得发白，熔在一起，冷却后成了一道凸起的接缝
scene: 修船厂的工人戴着面罩，蓝白色的火花沿着钢板接缝一路走过去。He welded a patch over the hole in the hull.
sceneCN: 这里 weld 是「焊接」（第 1 个义项：把金属边缘加热熔化后接合）；句意为他用焊补片把船壳的洞焊住。烧白后熔在一起的两块铁，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：焊接、熔接；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把一个社区紧密联结起来

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「焊工；焊接设备」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可焊接的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「焊接的；紧密结合的」

senses.title: To join metal by heat
senses.titleCN: 焊接：用高温把金属接合
senses.definition: to join pieces of metal by heating them until their edges melt and fuse
senses.definitionCN: 把金属件加热到边缘熔化、融合而接起来
senses.example: The two steel plates were welded along the seam.
senses.exampleCN: 两块钢板沿着接缝被焊在一起。
senses.why: The older sense of the word was to boil or to well up; heat joining two things grew from that image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词更早的意思是「沸腾、涌起」；以热把两件东西连成一体由此长成。

senses.title: To close a gap
senses.titleCN: 焊封：把裂缝或孔洞补上
senses.definition: to close a crack, hole or opening by welding material across it
senses.definitionCN: 用焊接材料把裂缝、孔洞或开口封住
senses.example: They welded the crack shut before the tank was filled.
senses.exampleCN: 油箱装油之前，他们先把裂缝焊封了。
senses.why: A hole is a place where two edges should meet; welding makes them meet again.
senses.whyCN: 孔洞本是两条边缘本该相接之处；焊接让它们重新接上。

senses.title: To unite things closely
senses.titleCN: 紧密结合：使事物连成一个整体
senses.definition: to join or unite things so that they act as one
senses.definitionCN: 把事物连成一体，使之作为一个整体运作
senses.example: Shared work welded the two teams into one group.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的工作把两个团队熔成了一个。
senses.why: The physical fusing is applied to people and plans: once welded, the parts no longer come apart easily.
senses.whyCN: 把熔接的物理过程用到人和计划上：一旦焊住，各部分便不易分开。

senses.title: The joint itself
senses.definition: the place or line where two pieces have been welded
senses.definitionCN: 两件东西被焊在一起的部位或线条
senses.example: Inspect the welds along the frame every year.
senses.exampleCN: 每年检查框架上的焊缝。
senses.why: The action freezes into a thing: what was a hot process is now a line you can inspect.
senses.whyCN: 动作凝固成事物：原本炽热的过程，如今成了可以检查的一条线。

senses.title: In technical compound uses
senses.definition: used in technical terms such as spot weld and weld neck flange
senses.definitionCN: 用于点焊、对焊法兰等技术术语
senses.example: A worker made four spot welds to hold the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 工人打了四个点焊把板子固定住。
senses.why: The trade builds its own fixed names, and weld becomes the second half of them.
senses.whyCN: 这一行当自造固定名称，weld 常居其后半。

intro.en: Weld began as a word for boiling and welling up, and only later became the metalworker's term.
intro.cn: weld 最初表示「沸腾、涌出」，后来才成了金属工的术语。

items.en: Wellan meant 'to boil, to well up', and it is the direct ancestor of the modern word.
items.cn: wellan 意为「沸腾、涌出」，是现代词形的直接祖先。

items.en: The past form and the noun were reinforced by Old Norse vella, which also meant to boil.
items.cn: 它的过去式与名词形式受到古诺尔斯语 vella 的加强，后者同样意为「沸腾」。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the verb was applied to metals heated until they joined, and the meaning shifted.
items.cn: 十六世纪，这个动词被用到加热至连接起来的金属上，词义随之转移。

items.en: Industry made it a craft noun: welder, welding, spot weld.
items.cn: 工业使它成了行当日用词：welder、welding、spot weld。

items.en: The figurative sense, to weld people or ideas together, followed from the physical one.
items.cn: 把人和观念「焊」在一起的比喻义，由物理义引申而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words easily confused with weld; the near-meaning group gathers ways of joining materials.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与 weld 混淆的词；近义组收各种连接材料的方式。

entries.definition: A person or machine that welds.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焊工」或「焊接设备」。

entries.definition: The act of holding and using a tool or power; from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挥动、运用」，出自另一个动词 wield。

entries.definition: An old word for a forested area; unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，古语指林区，与此词来源无关。

entries.definition: To join metal with a filler that melts at low heat; weaker than welding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「锡焊、软钎焊」，用低熔点填料，强度不如焊接。

entries.definition: To melt together into one; the general term for what welding does.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「熔合」，是表示焊接所做之事的通用词。

entries.definition: To stick things with an adhesive, not by heat.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用胶粘」，不靠热。

entries.definition: To join firmly, often used of materials and of people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「粘合、结合」，多用于材料与人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wellan and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wellan，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Weld began as boiling: two edges boil and run into one.
normal.cn: weld 起于沸腾：两条边缘烧到沸腾，于是连成一体。

normal.en: Weld together is the set phrase; the result is a welded joint.
normal.cn: weld together 是固定搭配，结果就是 welded joint「焊接接头」。

normal.en: Spot weld joins small points, not a whole seam.
normal.cn: spot weld 只焊几个点，不是整条缝。

normal.en: A welder wears a mask because the light is fierce.
normal.cn: 焊工戴面罩，因为弧光刺眼。

normal.en: Teams can be welded too: once joined, they act as one.
normal.cn: 团队也能被 weld：一旦接上，就像一个整体运作。

abstract.en: Picture two steel edges turning white, then running together and cooling into one raised seam.
abstract.cn: 想象两条钢边烧得发白，随后融为一体，冷却后留下一道凸起的接缝。

abstract.en: The word is about becoming one piece rather than being held together: that is why it is stronger than glue.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的是变成一整块，而不是被固定在一起：所以它比胶更牢。

abstract.en: Any two things that must never come apart can be described as welded.
abstract.cn: 任何再也不能分开的两样东西，都可以说成 welded。

examples.en: The workers welded the new beam to the old frame.
examples.cn: 工人把新梁焊到旧框架上。

examples.en: Their friendship was welded by a hard winter together.
examples.cn: 一起熬过的那个寒冬把他们的友谊焊得很牢。

examples.en: Check the welds for cracks after the winter.
examples.cn: 冬天过后检查焊缝有没有裂缝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威（weld）尔得」——威尔得师傅一烧一按，两块铁就长在一起：焊接

root: 古英语 wellan「沸腾、涌出」，受古诺尔斯语 vella 影响；十六世纪引申为把金属加热熔接；派生词有 welder、welding、weldable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weld start with heat joining two metal edges, then closing a gap, then binding people, then the joint itself, and finally its technical compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: weld 的五个义项从热把两条金属边接起开始，继而封住裂口、把人联结起来，再指焊出的接缝，最后是技术复合用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two steel edges glowing white, running together, cooling into one raised seam.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条钢边烧得发白，融为一体，冷却成一道凸起的接缝。

branches.en: HEAT LINE: the arc supplies the heat that lets the edges flow.
branches.cn: 热力线：电弧提供让边缘流动的热。

branches.en: GAP LINE: a crack is closed by filling it with molten metal.
branches.cn: 缺口线：用熔融金属把裂缝填上。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: the fusing is applied to teams and friendships.
branches.cn: 人物线：这种熔合被用到团队与友情上。

branches.en: SEAM LINE: the raised trace left when it cools.
branches.cn: 接缝线：冷却后留下的凸起痕迹。

branches.en: TRADE LINE: the craft adds names like spot weld.
branches.cn: 行业线：这一行当添出 spot weld 之类的名称。

intro.en: Weld is a native verb; its derivatives use the common English endings.
intro.cn: weld 是本族动词，派生词用常见的英语词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 福利；幸福；福利救济；（动物的）康乐
definition_en: the health and happiness of people, and the help the state gives to those in need
core_image: 社区服务站的窗口前排着队，柜台上摆着一叠表格和一支笔
scene: 社区服务站早上九点开门，窗口前排着队，有人来问孩子的补贴怎么申请。People come to the welfare office to ask about help with rent.
sceneCN: 这里 welfare 是「福利」（第 1 个义项：人的健康与幸福，以及由此而来的救济）；句意为人们到福利办事处询问房租方面的援助。排着队的窗口与一叠表格就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 福利；幸福；福利救济；康乐

senses.title: Health and happiness
senses.definition: the well-being of a person or group, in body and in life
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体在身体与生活上的良好状态
senses.example: Parents are responsible for their children’s welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 父母对孩子的生活安康负有责任。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense and still the widest: how well someone is doing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、也最宽泛的义项：一个人过得如何。

senses.title: State help for those in need
senses.definition: money or services given by the state to people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 国家给予需要者的钱款或服务
senses.example: The family lived on welfare for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人靠救济生活了两年。
senses.why: The general sense narrowed to the organised system that secures it.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛的义项收窄为保障它的那套制度。

senses.title: Organised care in a system
senses.definition: the whole set of policies and services for people’s well-being
senses.definitionCN: 为人的福祉而设的全部政策与服务
senses.example: The report compares welfare in five countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告比较了五个国家的福利制度。
senses.why: The personal good scaled up to a whole national arrangement, and the word followed it.
senses.whyCN: 个人的好处放大为整套国民安排，这个词也随之跟上。

senses.title: The good of animals
senses.definition: the condition of animals kept by people, especially farm animals
senses.definitionCN: 尤其是农场动物在人类饲养下的状况
senses.example: The farm was praised for its animal welfare standards.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场因动物福利标准受到称赞。
senses.why: The same care owed to people was extended to the animals people keep.
senses.whyCN: 原本对人负有的照料，被扩展到人所饲养的动物身上。

senses.title: A service for a group
senses.definition: used before a noun for services for students or workers
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指面向学生或职工的服务
senses.example: The union runs a welfare fund for members.
senses.exampleCN: 工会为会员设有一项福利基金。
senses.why: From the system came the smaller units that pay out, the fund and the office.
senses.whyCN: 从制度里长出付款的小单位：基金与办事处。

intro.en: Welfare is a modern compound of well and fare, literally the state of faring well, and it began in Middle English.
intro.cn: welfare 是 well 与 fare 的近代复合词，字面即「过得好」的状态，始于中古英语。

items.en: Fare meant to journey or to get on, so faring well meant prospering.
items.cn: fare 意为行走或进展，因此 faring well 就是过得兴旺。

items.en: Welfare first meant the condition of being happy and prosperous, close to our well-being.
items.cn: welfare 最初指幸福兴旺的状态，接近今天的 wellbeing。

items.en: As cities grew, welfare came to mean organised help for the poor.
items.cn: 随着城市发展，welfare 转而指对穷人的有组织帮助。

items.en: The welfare state made the word the name of a national system.
items.cn: 福利国家一词让这个词成为一种国民制度的名称。

items.en: Animal welfare extended it to creatures that cannot claim help themselves.
items.cn: animal welfare 把它扩展到无法自己主张帮助的生灵。

note.en: The first group is the welfare family, the second the nouns it is often set against.

entries.definition: Belief in state welfare provision.
Health and happiness in general.
Fare well, said at parting.
To get on, or the price of a journey.
Money paid by the state, or an advantage.
Help given voluntarily to those in need.
The state of being healthy and happy.
Looking after someone who needs it.

normalIntro.en: Welfare is plain English underneath: to fare well is to get on well, and welfare is that state.
normalIntro.cn: welfare 底下是很平常的英语：fare well 就是过得好，welfare 就是这个状态。

normal.en: Well plus fare: the fare is the travel, so fare well is to get on well.
normal.cn: well 加 fare：fare 是行走，fare well 就是走得顺。

normal.en: On welfare is American for living on benefit.
normal.cn: on welfare 是美式说法，指靠补助生活。

normal.en: The welfare state is the whole system, not one office.
normal.cn: the welfare state 是整套制度，不只是某个办事处。

normal.en: Well-being is the close twin; welfare took the official sense.
normal.cn: well-being 是近亲，welfare 承担了官方色彩。

normal.en: Animal welfare uses the same word for creatures kept by people.
normal.cn: animal welfare 用同一个词指人类饲养的动物。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a service-office window.
abstract.cn: 想服务窗口前排起的队。

abstract.en: Feel the edge of a form under your fingers.
abstract.cn: 感受指尖压着表格的硬边。

abstract.en: Hear a clerk explain a form line by line.
abstract.cn: 听窗口职员一行行解释表格。

examples.en: The school looks after the welfare of every pupil.
examples.cn: 学校关心每个学生的福祉。

examples.en: The new rules on animal welfare are stricter.
examples.cn: 新的动物福利规定更为严格。

examples.en: Many families depended on welfare during the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机期间许多家庭依赖救济。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维尔费」——维尔费先生在服务站排了队，他说这只为把日子过好一点。

root: well（古英语 wel，好）+ fare（古英语 faran，行走、进展）→ 中古英语 welfare；同根词有 farewell、well-being。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a condition of faring well, then names the help that secures it, the system that gives it, and finally the good of animals.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「过得好」的状态出发，继而为保障它的帮助、提供它的制度命名，最后扩展到动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue at a welfare office window.
core.cn: 核心意象：福利办事处窗口前的队伍。

branches.en: The well-being branch: parents responsible for a child.
branches.cn: 福祉分支：父母对孩子的责任。

branches.en: The help branch: a family living on welfare.
branches.cn: 救济分支：靠救济生活的家庭。

branches.en: The system branch: a report comparing five countries.
branches.cn: 制度分支：比较五国的报告。

branches.en: The animal and fund branch: farm standards and a union fund.
branches.cn: 动物与基金分支：农场标准与工会基金。

branches.en: The well-being and help branch: the same good, once described and once given.
branches.cn: 福祉与救济分支：同一份好，一处描述、一处给予。

intro.en: Welfare is a native compound of two Old English words and takes only the ordinary noun endings.
intro.cn: welfare 是两个古英语词的本土复合，只采用普通名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is English-built, so the Latin table is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语自造，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 鲸；鲸鱼；（口语）巨大的事物、极好的人
definition_en: a very large sea animal that breathes air through a hole on top of its head
core_image: 海面突然升起一股水柱，随后一段黑色的背脊慢慢滑过
scene: 船头的人忽然喊起来，远处海面喷起一道白色水柱，接着一段乌黑的背脊滑过水面。A whale surfaced beside the boat and blew a tall cloud of spray.
sceneCN: 这里 whale 是「鲸」（第 1 个义项：用头顶喷气孔呼吸的巨大海生动物）；句意为一头鲸在船边浮出水面，喷出高高的一团水雾。海面上腾起的水柱与滑过的黑背脊就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The great sea animal
senses.definition: a huge mammal that lives in the sea, breathes through a blowhole and feeds on small fish or plankton
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海中的巨大哺乳动物，用喷气孔呼吸，以小杂鱼或浮游生物为食
senses.example: A whale surfaced beside the boat and blew a tall cloud of spray.
senses.exampleCN: 一头鲸在船边浮出水面，喷出高高的一团水雾。
senses.why: The meaning of the animal is the only old sense of the word, and everything else in the entry grows out of it.
senses.whyCN: 指这种动物是这个词唯一古老的意思，词条中其余含义都由它长出。

senses.title: A very large example of something
senses.definition: in informal use, something remarkably large of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指同类中极大的东西
senses.example: The new library is a whale of a building.
senses.exampleCN: 新图书馆是一座庞然大物般的建筑。
senses.why: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived, so its name became a measure of sheer size.
senses.whyCN: 蓝鲸是有史以来最大的动物，于是它的名字成了纯粹大小的量尺。

senses.title: A very good person or thing
senses.definition: in phrases such as a whale of a time, someone or something outstanding
senses.definitionCN: 在 a whale of a time 等说法中，指非常出色的人或事
senses.example: The children had a whale of a time at the seaside.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在海边玩得非常尽兴。
senses.why: Great size shades into great quality, so the same animal name praises an experience instead of describing bulk.
senses.whyCN: 极大的体积会滑向极好的品质，于是同一个动物名从形容体量转为称赞体验。

senses.title: To hunt whales
senses.definition: in the verb use, to hunt whales, now usually only in historical or critical text
senses.definitionCN: 动词用法，指捕猎鲸鱼，现多见于历史叙述或批评语境
senses.example: Several nations sailed south to whale in those waters.
senses.exampleCN: 当时有几个国家南下到那片海域捕鲸。
senses.why: English turns a hunted animal into a verb, so whale means the hunt and whaling means the industry.
senses.whyCN: 英语会把被猎的动物变成动词，于是 whale 指捕猎，whaling 指这门行业。

intro.en: Whale comes from Old English hwæl, a word shared with Old Norse and the other Germanic languages, and it has meant this animal and nothing else for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: whale 源自古英语 hwæl，与古诺斯语及其他日耳曼语共有，一千多年来一直指这种动物，别无他义。

items.en: The root probably named the animal by its rolling or blowing look, though the exact picture is lost.
items.cn: 这个词根大概按动物翻滚或喷水的样子来命名，但确切画面已失。

items.en: Hwæl appears in early poetry for the whale as the great fish of the open sea.
items.cn: hwæl 出现在早期诗歌中，指开阔海面上的巨鱼。

items.en: Norse settlers and sailors brought forms such as hvalr, and northern English kept the wh sound.
items.cn: 诺斯定居者与船员带来 hvalr 等形式，英格兰北部保留了 wh 的读音。

items.en: The spelling settled as whal, later whale, and whaling grew into a whole northern industry.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 whal，后作 whale，捕鲸业在北方发展成完整产业。

items.en: The huge size of the animal gave the casual phrases a whale of a time and a whale of a building.
items.cn: 这种动物的巨大体形带来了 a whale of a time、a whale of a building 这类口语说法。

note.en: The first group gathers words that are confused with whale in spelling, the second the sea animals and the words for bigness.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写容易与 whale 相混的词，第二组收海洋动物与表示巨大的说法。

entries.definition: To cry out with a long sad sound, pronounced the same.
entries.definitionCN: 哀号；恸哭，与 whale 同音

entries.definition: A round object that turns, with a different vowel.
During the time that, written almost the same.
The stiff plates from a whale's mouth.
A smaller sea mammal that also breathes through a hole on top.
A large fish with sharp teeth, often confused with the whale in old stories.
The class the whale belongs to, since it feeds its young on milk.
Something enormously large, the idea behind the casual sense.

normalIntro.en: The word is almost a picture of the animal: a wide w for the body, and a long tail of letters after the vowel.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词几乎就是这动物的画像：宽宽的 w 是身体，元音后面拖一条长尾巴。

normal.en: Whale and wail sound the same; one blows water, the other blows noise.
normal.cn: whale 与 wail 同音：一个喷水柱，一个喷哭声。

normal.en: The wh- spelling is old English: who, what, where, whale.
normal.cn: wh- 的拼写很古老：who、what、where、whale 都是。

normal.en: A blue whale is bigger than any dinosaur, which is why its name means huge.
normal.cn: 蓝鲸比任何恐龙都大，所以它的名字才代表巨大。

normal.en: Whaling is the industry, whaler is the ship, whalebone is the material.
normal.cn: whaling 是行业，whaler 是船，whalebone 是材料。

normal.en: A whale of a time means a very good time, not a wet one.
normal.cn: a whale of a time 指非常尽兴，而不是湿淋淋。

abstract.en: Feel the deck shake as something huge passes under it.
abstract.cn: 感觉船甲板在某个巨物从下面经过时发颤。

abstract.en: See a white column stand still in the air for a moment.
abstract.cn: 看一根白色水柱在空中短暂地立住。

abstract.en: Hear a low sound travel a long way through water.
abstract.cn: 听一个低沉的声音在水里传出很远。

examples.en: Whales come to these waters every winter to feed.
examples.cn: 每年冬天鲸都会到这片海域来觅食。

examples.en: People once hunted the animal for its oil, so whaling was a hard trade.
examples.cn: 人们曾为取油而捕杀这种动物，因此捕鲸是一桩艰苦的行当。

examples.en: We had a whale of a time at your party.
examples.cn: 我们在你的聚会上玩得非常尽兴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂了」——喂了它一桶小鱼，鲸就浮上来喷了一道水柱。

root: 古英语 hwæl（鲸）→ 中古英语 whal → whale；与古诺斯语 hvalr 同源，同族有 whaling、whaler、whalebone。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the animal first, then its enormous size turns into a casual word for anything huge, then into praise, and the verb names the hunt.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指这种动物，接着它巨大的体型变成了指任何庞然大物的口语，再变成赞语，最后动词形式指捕猎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white column of spray over a black back.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑色背脊上方一道白色水柱。

branches.en: The animal branch: a whale surfacing beside the boat.
branches.cn: 动物分支：船边浮出的鲸。

branches.en: The size branch: a whale of a building.
branches.cn: 体量分支：庞然大物般的建筑。

branches.en: The praise branch: a whale of a time at the party.
branches.cn: 赞语分支：聚会上玩得尽兴。

branches.en: The hunting branch: nations sailing south to whale.
branches.cn: 捕猎分支：各国南下捕鲸。

branches.en: The naming branch: whalebone and whale watching built on the animal itself.
branches.cn: 命名分支：鲸须与观鲸都建立在动物本身之上。

intro.en: Whale is a simple Germanic noun, and the family grows through -ing, -er and the compound ending -bone.
intro.cn: whale 是简单的日耳曼语名词，词族靠 -ing、-er 以及复合词尾 -bone 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin named the animal cetus or ballaena; the second of these passed through Greek into scientific words, so the Latin entries below are cognate labels rather than ancestors of whale.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 cetus 或 ballaena 指鲸；后者经由希腊语进入科学术语，所以下面的拉丁条目只是同类标签，并非 whale 的祖先。

items.example: It is both a noun and a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded shape.
items.exampleCN: 它是最早有记录的词形。

items.meaning: a person or ship that does
the stiff plates of the mouth

items.example: It is a modern tourist phrase.
It carries the size sense into praise.
items.exampleCN: 它把体量义带进赞语里。

definition_zh: 然而；而；（法律）鉴于
definition_en: used to compare two facts and show that they differ, or at the start of a legal statement to give a reason
core_image: 两只手各拿一张卡片，卡片上的字正好相反
scene: 两个学生在讨论，一人举起一张卡片：一张写着「快」，一张写着「准」。The north is wet and green, whereas the south is dry and stony.
sceneCN: 这里 whereas 是「然而、而」（第 1 个义项：对比两个事实并显示其差别）；句意为北方湿润青绿，而南方干燥多石。两张字面相反的卡片并排举起，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: In contrast to that
senses.definition: used to introduce a fact that is different from or opposite to the one just stated
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个与刚说过的事实不同或相反的事实
senses.example: The north is wet and green, whereas the south is dry and stony.
senses.exampleCN: 北方湿润青绿，而南方干燥多石。
senses.why: Where once meant at the point that, and adding so or as sharpened the two points into a contrast.
senses.whyCN: where 本指「在…这一点上」，加上 so 或 as 之后，两个点被磨成了一对对照。

senses.title: Because in fact
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause in legal and official texts to state a fact that explains a rule
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与公文文本的条款开头陈述一个解释规则的事实
senses.example: Whereas the tenant has paid the rent in full, this agreement is now complete.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴于承租人已全额付清租金，本协议现已履行完毕。
senses.why: Legal drafts use the word because one clause is set against the next, and the contrast hardened into a stated ground.
senses.whyCN: 法律草案使用此词，是因为一条条款总是对着下一条，这种对照就硬化成陈述的理由。

senses.title: While it is true that
senses.definition: used in careful argument to admit one fact before giving a qualification
senses.definitionCN: 在严谨论述中先承认一个事实，再给出限定
senses.example: Whereas the plan is cheap, it will take years to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划虽然便宜，却要花好几年才能完成。
senses.why: A contrast between two clauses can lean towards concession when the second clause weakens the first.
senses.whyCN: 两句之间的对照在第二句削弱第一句时，就会偏向让步。

intro.en: Whereas began in Middle English as where plus so, then where as, with the meaning at which place or in which case.
intro.cn: whereas 在中古英语中本是 where 加 so，后作 where as，意思是「在何处」或「在何种情况下」。

items.en: The parts hwær and swā were separate and simply meant where and so.
items.cn: hwær 与 swā 两个成分彼此分开，只表示「何地」和「如此」。

items.en: The phrase where so narrowed to where as and came to mark a condition or a case.
items.cn: 短语 where so 收窄成 where as，用来标记条件或情形。

items.en: Legal drafts adopted whereas to open each recital, and that use fixed the word in official English.
items.cn: 法律草案采用 whereas 作为每段陈述的开头，这一用法把这个词固定在官方英语里。

items.en: In ordinary prose the legal flavour faded and the word became a plain marker of contrast.
items.cn: 在普通文章里法律的意味淡去，这个词成了单纯的对照标记。

items.en: Modern editors often prefer while or but, and whereas now sounds slightly formal.
items.cn: 现代编辑往往更爱用 while 或 but，如今 whereas 听起来略显正式。

note.en: The first group gathers the contrast words that are easily exchanged with whereas, the second the legal and concessive relatives.
note.cn: 第一组收容易与 whereas 互换的对照词，第二组收法律与让步的相关说法。

entries.definition: The everyday word for contrast, softer than whereas.
entries.definitionCN: 而；虽然，比 whereas 更日常

entries.definition: The base word, which asks about place.
The plainest contrast word in English.
The -ever member of the same family.
By which, a legal cousin of whereas.
On which, another formal relative.
The plain concession word that matches the third sense.

normalIntro.en: The word is literally where plus as, so it means in the place or case where something else is true.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是 where 加 as，意思是「在某事成立的这一边」。

normal.en: Split it as where + as, and hear the two halves of a comparison.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 where + as，就听见一个比较的两半。

normal.en: The legal whereas at the start of a contract is a reason, not a contrast.
normal.cn: 合同开头那个法律用的 whereas 是理由，不是对照。

normal.en: While is the everyday twin; whereas is the formal one.
normal.cn: while 是日常的双胞胎，whereas 是正式的那个。

normal.en: A semicolon before whereas, and a comma after it, is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: whereas 前用分号、后用逗号是常见格局。

normal.en: Whereas never joins two equal points; it puts them on opposite sides.
normal.cn: whereas 从不把两点放在同一边，而是分放两侧。

abstract.en: See two cards held up with opposite words.
abstract.cn: 看两张卡片被举起，写着相反的字。

abstract.en: Feel a scale tip from one clause to the other.
abstract.cn: 感受天平从一个分句倒向另一个。

abstract.en: Hear the dry voice of a contract being read.
abstract.cn: 听合同被念出来时那种干涩的声音。

examples.en: Some students study best in the morning, whereas others work late at night.
examples.cn: 有些学生早晨效率最高，而另一些人则深夜苦干。

examples.en: Whereas the old road was narrow, the new one has four lanes.
examples.cn: 旧路很窄，而新路有四条车道。

examples.en: Whereas the company has paid all fees, this licence is valid.
examples.cn: 鉴于该公司已付清全部费用，本许可证有效。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔阿兹」——威尔说东，阿兹说西：然而两人说的完全不同。

root: 中古英语 where so / where as → 现代英语 whereas；同族有 where、whereby、whereon。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as where plus so, tightens into a marker of contrast, hardens into a legal reason, and softens into concession.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从 where 加 so 开始，收窄成对照标记，硬化成法律上的理由，又能软化为让步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cards held side by side with opposite words.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张写着相反字样的卡片并排举起。

branches.en: The contrast branch: wet in the north, whereas dry in the south.
branches.cn: 对照分支：北方湿，而南方干。

branches.en: The legal branch: whereas the tenant has paid the rent.
branches.cn: 法律分支：鉴于承租人已付租金。

branches.en: The concession branch: whereas the plan is cheap, it is slow.
branches.cn: 让步分支：计划虽便宜，却很慢。

branches.en: The register branch: whereas sounding formal next to while.
branches.cn: 语体分支：与 while 相比 whereas 更正式。

branches.en: The drafting branch: each recital opening with whereas.
branches.cn: 起草分支：每段陈述以 whereas 开头。

intro.en: Whereas is a fixed compound of where and as, and it no longer takes new endings; its closest relatives are whereby and whereon.
intro.cn: whereas 是 where 与 as 的固定复合词，不再接新词尾；最近的相关词是 whereby 与 whereon。

latinIntro.en: Latin marked the same contrast with autem and vero, and legal Latin used cum or quoniam for the reason clause; those are parallels, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 autem 与 vero 标记同样的对照，法律拉丁语用 cum 或 quoniam 引出理由从句；这些都是并行说法，不是祖源。

items.meaning: in what place, in which case
items.example: It is the first half of the word.
It marks the next event in a narrative.
items.exampleCN: 它标记叙述中的紧接事件。

items.meaning: although, and at the same time

items.example: It carries the contrast in whereas.
items.exampleCN: 它在 whereas 中承载对照。

latinEntries.meaning: however, but on the other hand

definition_zh: 当…的时候；虽然；然而；（一段时间）一会儿
definition_en: during the time that something happens, and also used to contrast two facts or to name a short period of time
core_image: 两条平行的钟表指针同时走着，一条走完另一条还在动
scene: 厨房里水在烧，她一边等一边切菜，两个动作同时进行。She read the paper while the water was boiling.
sceneCN: 这里 while 是「当…的时候」（第 1 个义项：在某事进行的那段时间里）；句意为水开的时候她在看报纸。两条平行走的指针同时指着的画面就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: During the time that
senses.definition: used to say that one thing happens during the same period as another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一件事与另一件事发生在同一段时间内
senses.example: She read the paper while the water was boiling.
senses.exampleCN: 水开的时候她在看报纸。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a stretch of time, and a clause placed inside that stretch gives the during meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思只是一段时间，把从句放进这段时间里就产生了「当…时」的意思。

senses.title: Although
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to admit a fact that makes the main point surprising
senses.definitionCN: 用在从句开头，承认一个使主句令人意外的事实
senses.example: While the plan is cheap, it will take years to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划虽然便宜，却要花好几年才能完成。
senses.why: Two things placed side by side invite comparison, and when the second weakens the first the word leans to although.
senses.whyCN: 两件事并排摆放就会引来比较，当第二件削弱第一件时，这个词便偏向 although。

senses.title: Whereas
senses.definition: used to compare two facts and show that they are different
senses.definitionCN: 比较两个事实，显示二者不同
senses.example: Some people talk a lot, while others say nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人话很多，而另一些人什么都不说。
senses.why: The same side-by-side picture becomes a plain contrast when the two facts are simply weighed against each other.
senses.whyCN: 同样是并排的画面，当两个事实只是彼此对照时，就成了单纯的对比。

senses.title: A period of time
senses.definition: a short period of time, usually after the words a or for
senses.definitionCN: 一小段时间，通常跟在 a 或 for 之后
senses.example: Wait here for a while and I will be back.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里等一会儿，我就回来。
senses.why: This is the noun behind the conjunction: a while is the stretch of time that the clause later filled in.
senses.whyCN: 这是连词背后的名词：a while 就是后来被从句填进去的那段时间。

senses.title: To pass time pleasantly
senses.definition: in while away, to spend time in a relaxed way until it has passed
senses.definitionCN: 在 while away 中，指轻松地度过一段时间
senses.example: We whiled away the afternoon on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海滩上打发了整个下午。
senses.why: If a while is a block of time, then while away is the act of letting that block be used up.
senses.whyCN: 如果 a while 是一块时间，那么 while away 就是让那块时间被用掉的动作。

intro.en: While began as the Old English noun hwīl, a period of time, and only later became the conjunction that fills such a period.
intro.cn: while 起初是古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间），后来才成为填充这段时间的连词。

items.en: The stem hwī- meant a rest or a span of time in the older Germanic languages.
items.cn: 在较早的日耳曼语中，词干 hwī- 指一段休息或一段时间。

items.en: Hwīl was a noun, and the phrase þā hwīle þe, the time that, was its full form.
items.cn: hwīl 是名词，完整形式是 þā hwīle þe，意思是「…的那段时间」。

items.en: The long phrase shrank to while that and then to plain while, which took over the conjunction job.
items.cn: 长短语缩短为 while that，再缩成 while，连词职能便由它承担。

items.en: While spread into contrast and concession, replacing older words in ordinary prose.
items.cn: while 扩展到对比与让步，在普通文章中取代了更早的说法。

items.en: The noun survives in a while, once in a while and while away, keeping the original time sense.
items.cn: 名词义保存在 a while、once in a while 与 while away 中，保留了最初的时间意味。

note.en: The first group is the words one letter away in shape, the second the time and contrast words that do the same work.
note.cn: 第一组是字形只差一点的词，第二组是承担同样职能的时间与转折词。

entries.definition: A very large sea animal, one letter longer.
The same word with a t, common in British prose.
A trick, and the same shape as the verb in while away.
A high complaining sound.
The preposition version of the same time relation.
Two things happening at the same moment.
The full concession word behind sense two.
The formal contrast partner of while.

normalIntro.en: Hold two films running side by side, and while is the word that ties their frames together.
normalIntro.cn: 想两部并排播放的影片，while 就是把两边的画面绑在一起的那个词。

normal.en: A while is a block of time, so the conjunction simply puts a clause inside the block.
normal.cn: a while 是一块时间，连词就是把从句放进这块时间里。

normal.en: Side by side can mean at the same time, in contrast, or in spite of.
normal.cn: 并排既可以是同时，也可以是对比，还可以是让步。

normal.en: While away means letting the block of time run out pleasantly.
normal.cn: while away 是让那块时间愉快地流走。

normal.en: British writing adds a t and says whilst; ordinary speech does not.
normal.cn: 英式书面语加个 t 说 whilst，日常口语则不这样用。

normal.en: After a comma, while begins the second of two weighed facts.
normal.cn: 在逗号之后，while 引出两个被比较事实中的第二个。

abstract.en: See two clock hands turning at the same pace.
abstract.cn: 想两根同时同速转动的钟表指针。

abstract.en: Hear water boiling under a quiet page turning.
abstract.cn: 听水开的声响下面是翻书声。

abstract.en: Feel a stretch of time with nothing urgent in it.
abstract.cn: 感受一段没有急事的时光。

examples.en: He called while I was cooking dinner.
examples.cn: 我做晚饭的时候他打来了电话。

examples.en: While I agree with you, I cannot support this plan.
examples.cn: 虽然我同意你的看法，却无法支持这个计划。

examples.en: Let us rest for a while before we continue.
examples.cn: 我们歇一会儿再继续吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外欧」——望外一瞧，时间悄悄流过去一会儿。

root: 古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间）→ 中古英语 while；同族有 whilst、meanwhile、worthwhile。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a block of time, then fills that block with a clause, then weighs two clauses, and finally keeps the plain noun in a while and while away.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一块时间开始，用从句把这块时间填满，再让两个从句相互权衡，最后把朴素的名词义留在 a while 与 while away 里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two clock hands moving side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根并排走动的钟表指针。

branches.en: The simultaneity branch: boiling water and a newspaper.
branches.cn: 同时分支：烧水与看报。

branches.en: The concession branch: while the plan is cheap, it is slow.
branches.cn: 让步分支：计划虽便宜，却很慢。

branches.en: The contrast branch: some talk, while others say nothing.
branches.cn: 对比分支：有人话多，有人沉默。

branches.en: The noun branch: wait for a while.
branches.cn: 名词分支：等一会儿。

branches.en: The phrasal branch: whiling away an afternoon.
branches.cn: 短语分支：打发一个下午。

intro.en: While is a free Old English word; its family is made by compounds such as meanwhile and by the old -st form whilst.
intro.cn: while 是古英语的自由词；它的词族由 meanwhile 这类复合词和古老的 -st 形式 whilst 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin covered the same ground with dum and interim; the entries below are parallel forms, not the source of while.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 dum 与 interim 表达同样的意思；下面的条目是平行形式，并非 while 的来源。

items.example: It works as noun and conjunction.
items.exampleCN: 它既可作名词也可作连词。

items.example: It keeps the old noun alive.
items.exampleCN: 它让古老的名词义活下来。

items.example: It repeats the noun in idiom.
items.exampleCN: 它在习语中重复这个名词。

items.example: It turns time into a verb.
It is the bridge to the conjunction.

definition_zh: 旋风；尘卷风；一连串迅疾的事件；情绪翻涌
definition_en: a mass of air turning rapidly around a moving centre, often lifting dust or loose material
core_image: 干草场上，风把尘土和草屑拧成一根旋转的柱子，贴着地面横冲过去
scene: 麦场上，一阵风把干草和尘土卷成一根旋转的柱子，老人指着说 A whirlwind crossed the yard and carried the straw over the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 whirlwind 指「绕移动中心快速旋转的气团」（第 1 个义项：能把尘土和轻物卷起的旋风）；句意为一阵旋风穿过院子，把稻草卷过了篱笆。

pos.zh: 旋风；尘卷风；一连串迅疾之事
旋风式的；极快的（如旋风式旅行）

collocations.zh: 旋风式旅行；走马观花的一趟
自食其果；收获自己种下的恶果

derivatives.zh: 旋风式旅行；行程极紧的访问

senses.title: Air turning rapidly around a centre
senses.titleCN: 旋风：绕中心快速旋转的气团
senses.definition: a body of air turning rapidly around a centre that moves across the ground
senses.definitionCN: 绕一个中心快速旋转、并沿地面移动的气团
senses.example: A whirlwind scattered the dry leaves across the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵旋风把干叶子吹散到公路上。
senses.why: Whirl names the turning and wind names the air, so the compound says exactly what it is: air that spins.
senses.whyCN: whirl 说「转」，wind 说「空气」，复合词正好说出它是什么：会转的空气。

senses.title: Dust devil
senses.titleCN: 尘卷风：看得见的尘土柱
senses.definition: a small, short-lived vortex made visible by the dust and debris it lifts
senses.definitionCN: 因卷起尘土与碎屑而可见的小型短命涡旋
senses.example: Dust devils danced along the empty road at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时分，尘卷风在空荡的公路上跳跃。
senses.why: Once the vortex lifts loose material, the dust draws its outline, and the word names that visible column.
senses.whyCN: 涡旋卷起松软物质后，尘土勾出它的轮廓，这个词就指那根可见的柱子。

senses.title: A violent tornado-scale vortex
senses.definition: in older and literary usage, a large destructive whirlwind capable of tearing roofs away
senses.definitionCN: 在较早与文学用法中，指能掀掉屋顶的大型破坏性旋风
senses.example: The whirlwind tore the roof off the barn and flung it into the creek.
senses.exampleCN: 旋风掀掉谷仓的屋顶，把它甩进小河。
senses.why: Before tornado became the technical term, whirlwind covered the violent end of the scale, and the older sense survives in literature.
senses.whyCN: 在 tornado 成为术语之前，whirlwind 涵盖这一暴力极端，旧义仍留在文学中。

senses.title: Rapid succession of events
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：一连串迅疾的事件
senses.definition: a rapid, dizzying succession of events that leaves little time to rest
senses.definitionCN: 一连串迅速而令人眩晕、几乎没有喘息时间的事件
senses.example: The wedding was a whirlwind of meetings, forms and last-minute repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼成了一连串会面、表格与临时修补。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the spin: events arrive faster than they can be sorted, the way dust is swept up.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了旋转：事件来得比理清更快，就像尘土被卷起。

senses.title: Emotional turmoil
senses.definition: a confused, intense swirl of feelings that carries a person along
senses.definitionCN: 把人带着走的一团混乱而强烈的情绪
senses.example: She left the interview in a whirlwind of relief and doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着宽慰与怀疑交织的翻涌情绪离开了面试。
senses.why: Feelings are described as air in motion: they circle, collide and refuse to settle.
senses.whyCN: 情绪被说成流动的空气：打转、相撞、不肯平息。

senses.title: Very fast, as an attributive
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：极快的、旋风式的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean very fast and tightly packed, as in a whirlwind tour
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示极快且安排密集，如旋风式旅行
senses.example: They did a whirlwind tour of three capitals in five days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们五天内旋风式地游了三座首都。
senses.why: The speed of the vortex becomes the defining quality of the trip, so the noun turns into a modifier.
senses.whyCN: 涡旋的速度成了这趟旅行的定义特征，于是名词变成修饰语。

senses.title: Biblical and literary tempest
senses.definition: a destructive tempest used as an image of judgment, as in the phrase reap the whirlwind
senses.definitionCN: 作为审判意象的破坏性暴风，如短语「自食其果」所示
senses.example: The prophet warned that the nation would reap the whirlwind.
senses.exampleCN: 先知警告说，这个民族将自食其果。
senses.why: Scriptural language uses the storm as a picture of consequences arriving with irresistible force.
senses.whyCN: 圣经语言用风暴比喻以不可阻挡之势到来的后果。

senses.title: A swirling mass of loose material
senses.definition: the swirling load itself, such as leaves, dust or flame carried up in a circle
senses.definitionCN: 被卷起旋转的物质本身，如树叶、尘土或火焰
senses.example: A whirlwind of leaves followed the children down the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 一团旋转的树叶跟着孩子们跑下小径。
senses.why: The container and the contents trade places: the wind is named by the visible mass it carries.
senses.whyCN: 容器与内容互换：风用它携带的可见物质来命名。

intro.en: Whirlwind is a native English compound of whirl and wind. Whirl came from Old Norse, wind from Old English; the compound is recorded from the fourteenth century, and the figurative use is later.
intro.cn: whirlwind 是英语本土复合词，由 whirl 与 wind 合成。whirl 来自古诺斯语，wind 来自古英语；复合词约 14 世纪见于记载，比喻用法更晚。

items.en: Old Norse hvirfla meant 'to turn round, whirl', and the noun hvirfill named a ring, a circle or a whirlpool.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hvirfla 意为「旋转、打转」，名词 hvirfill 指环、圆圈或漩涡。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as *hwerb- or *hwerfl- 'to turn'; German wirbeln 'to whirl' and Dutch wervelen descend from the same reconstructed form.
items.cn: 更早的祖形被重构为 *hwerb- 或 *hwerfl-，意为「转」；德语 wirbeln「旋转」与荷兰语 wervelen 都出自同一重构形式。

items.en: Old English wind 'wind' goes back to Proto-Germanic *windaz, generally connected with a root meaning 'to blow'.
items.cn: 古英语 wind「风」上溯到原始日耳曼语 *windaz，一般与表示「吹」的词根相联系。

items.en: The compound whirlwind is recorded in Middle English; the exact first occurrence is uncertain, and the word competed with other native terms for the same weather.
items.cn: 复合词 whirlwind 见于中古英语；确切的最早书证不确定，这个词曾与其他本土说法竞争同一天气现象。

items.en: The figurative senses, a whirlwind of events and a whirlwind tour, belong to later literary and journalistic usage.
items.cn: 比喻义——一连串事件与旋风式旅行——属于较晚的文学与新闻用法。

note.en: The first group is built from the same or similar pieces but means something else; the second group holds the rotating-weather family.
note.cn: 第一组由相同或相近的成分构成，但意思不同；第二组是旋转天气家族。

entries.definition: A building with sails turned by the wind to grind grain or pump water; the second element is a machine, not spinning air.
entries.definitionCN: 用风转动叶片来磨粮或抽水的建筑；第二成分是机器，不是旋转的空气。

entries.definition: From Old Norse vindauga 'wind eye', an opening for air and light; it shares wind but not the whirling.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古诺斯语 vindauga「风眼」，通风透光的开口；同有 wind，但没有旋转义。

entries.definition: A spinning body of water; the same whirl element with pool instead of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 旋转的水体；同一 whirl 成分，但换成 pool 而非 wind。

entries.definition: The present participle of the verb whirl 'to turn quickly'; it describes the action, not the weather system.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 whirl「快速旋转」的现在分词；描述动作，不是天气系统。

entries.definition: The technical term for a violent vortex touching the ground from a thundercloud; narrower and more formal than whirlwind.
entries.definitionCN: 从雷暴云触地的猛烈涡旋的技术术语；比 whirlwind 更窄、更正式。

entries.definition: A large low-pressure system whose winds rotate around a centre; far larger than a whirlwind.
entries.definitionCN: 风绕中心旋转的大型低压系统；比旋风大得多。

entries.definition: The usual name for a small, fair-weather whirlwind made visible by dust.
entries.definitionCN: 晴好天气下由尘土显形的小型旋风的常用名称。

entries.definition: A sudden brief increase in wind; it pushes in a straight line rather than turning in a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 风的突然短暂加强；是直线推进而非绕圈旋转。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound, real fixed phrases and the real rotating-weather family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词两个真实成分、真实固定搭配与真实旋转天气词族，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: whirl 'turn quickly' + wind 'moving air': the word is its own definition.
normal.cn: whirl「快转」+ wind「流动的空气」：这个词就是自己的定义。

normal.en: The same whirl sits in whirlpool and whirligig.
normal.cn: 同一个 whirl 在 whirlpool 与 whirligig 里。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: whirlwind tour, whirlwind romance, whirlwind of change.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：旋风式旅行、闪电式恋情、急剧变化。

normal.en: Reap the whirlwind means suffer the consequences of what you did.
normal.cn: reap the whirlwind 意为自食其果。
